content.text:
I added 13 cases to `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py`, so the suite now has 22. The counts below are from the first full baseline: the current prompt, unchanged, 20 runs per case.

**Change conversation, about a saved Anycubic Kobra 3 (a print host, not connected)**

| Case | The person says | Passes when | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `change-ask-start-gcode` | "what's the current start g-code?" | Nothing is added or changed, and the reply neither treats the printer as not yet added nor says it must be connected to see the setting (judge) | 19/20 |
| `change-ask-nozzle` | "what nozzle size is it set up for?" | The reply says 0.4 and nothing changes | 20/20 |
| `change-loaded-filament` | "I just loaded black PETG" | Nothing is saved | 19/20 → 20/20 after a check fix |
| `change-plate` | "I switched to the textured PEI plate" | Nothing is saved | 20/20 |
| `change-unshipped-nozzle` | "I put a 0.3 nozzle on it" | Nothing is saved, and the reply names 0.2, 0.4, 0.6 and 0.8 | 20/20 |
| `change-then-connect` | "can you connect it…?", then "it's at 192.168.1.42" | The model asks for the address instead of making one up, then the connect card opens for that address | 20/20 |

**Change conversation, about a connected Bambu Lab A1 mini holding PLA and PETG**

| Case | The person says | Passes when | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `change-ask-loaded` | "what filament is loaded right now?" | The reply names both materials | 20/20 |

**Connect conversation**

| Case | Setup | Passes when | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `connect-host-address` | A Voron; the person says "http://voron.local, I open it with Mainsail" | The card opens for Moonraker at that address | 20/20 |
| `connect-bambu-not-found` | An A1 mini with no printer in LAN mode on the network | The status is checked, no card opens, and the reply points to LAN mode (judge) | 20/20 |
| `connect-ask-why` | "do I have to connect it? what do I get from that?" | Nothing runs, and the reply says connecting is optional (judge) | 19/20 |

**Add conversation**

| Case | The person says | Passes when | Baseline |
|---|---|---|---|
| `add-vague-description` | "the small bambu one" | Nothing is added before they confirm | 19/20 |
| `add-unsupported-printer` | "an Elegoo Saturn 4 Ultra" (resin) | Nothing is shown or added, and no other model is offered instead (judge) | 19/20 → 20/20 after a check fix |
| `add-ask-start-gcode` | The start g-code question, before any printer exists | Nothing is added, and the reply asks which printer they have (judge) | 15/20 with the old check; the 5 failures were the check's fault |

**Checks that apply to every reply in every case, old and new:**
- The reply's "Choices:" line must be one the page draws correctly: on the last line, 2–4 choices, each under 30 characters, or Done on its own.
- The reply must not contain internal words: profile, preset, catalog, or a tool's name.

The 9 original cases passed 20/20 each, except one network error in `add-not-now-done`.

**Real failures in the baseline:**
- `change-ask-start-gcode` run 16: "…or we can set up this printer first". That is the reported bug.
- `add-vague-description` run 20: offered 5 choices, where the limit is 4.
- `connect-ask-why` run 8: "easily.Choices: …" with no space before "Choices:", so the page shows it as plain text.

**Changes to the harness after the first run:**
- `add-ask-start-gcode` now uses a judge question instead of looking for a "?". Replies like "Tell me the brand and model" do ask.
- I removed a "Done must be alone" check that I had invented; the prompt doesn't forbid "Connect it | Done".
- The harness now retries a dropped connection.

The rerun with those changes was cut off after three cases (add-ask-start-gcode 19/20, add-choose-from-three 20/20, add-named-model 19/20). I haven't read the failed transcripts for that run yet. So there is no complete baseline from the final checks, and I need to run the full suite again before any prompt change is compared against it.

I also updated the harness README with the new cases and checks. Nothing is committed.

content.text:
Yes. Before I started, the system prompt already had tests at four levels. Only the first of them measures what the model actually does.

**1. Live-model cases, `tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py` (the harness I extended)**
Nine cases, all on the main paths: `connect-bambu`, `add-named-model`, `add-choose-from-three`, `add-then-undo`, `add-not-now-done`, `connect-verified-done`, `connect-leave-done`, `connect-after-question` and `change-nozzle-done`. Each was added along with the prompt rule it guards. The README records the before and after counts, for example the undo rule going from 3/20 to 20/20. Every one passed 20/20 in my baseline, apart from one network error. Change mode had just one case, on its expected path, and no case asked a question the tools can't answer.

**2. Unit tests on the prompt text, `AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.test.ts` (vitest)**
These run no model; they check the rendered text:
- Add mode carries every printer, one line each.
- The facts about the printer are stated as they are now.
- The missing plug-in is stated when the app says so.
- A printer that isn't connected isn't said to have anything loaded, and a connected one that reports nothing says so.
- Printers found on the network are listed.
- Rules that encode real constraints are still present.
- No button, screen or form is named.
- The Choices examples parse as the page parses them.

The same file includes a "printer evaluation writer". It isn't a check: it fills the page's instructions into request files the C++ side writes.

**3. C++ tests on how the app handles the prompt, `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp`**
- The instructions are the page's words.
- A new session waits for new ones.
- Oversized text is refused.
- `[.printer-eval]` is hidden unless asked for; it writes out the Add and Change request files for an offline evaluation.

**4. The real app, driven by the live model: `shell_harness --printer-live`**
It runs the handoff's worked examples through the actual panel. That includes a change sequence on "Lab Printer": an unsure nozzle swap, "i put a 0.6 nozzle on it", putting it back, hardened steel, the plate, and 0.3. It checks what was actually saved. It needs a full app build, and I didn't run it.

I also saw a pointer to an older identification evaluation in `agent-docs/jusprin/spikes/printer-identify/`: word and photo test sets for picking a printer model. It isn't in this worktree; the docs call it uncommitted.

None of these covered the Kobra 3 situation, a question outside the tools in a change conversation, or any other off-path request. That gap is what the 13 new cases fill.

ok you extend the right harness.

Now do these:

* make sure existing test cases stays.
* check the git log for what changes have been made to printer instructions, and to fix what problems. If you can identify the test cases for these problems to prevent regression, also add them.
* reduce the number of runs. 20 seems like a lot. I'm hoping it won't take more than 100 runs in total every time we run the harness. so if we have 20 test cases in total, let's have 5 runs for each of them
Starting with the history of the printer instructions to see which problems each change fixed.

=== 0e55c4f9be Talk to the agent about a printer, where the printers column is
"+ Add printer" on Home opened a modal dialog that ran a fixed recognition
script against OpenAI, and "Printer settings…" opened OrcaSlicer's own settings
window. Both now open a conversation in Home's printers column: the Prepare
screen's panel, with a printer session behind it, so the same agent both adds a
printer and changes one. Wireframe 19b, decided on turn 19.

The session is its own, not the project's. AgentHost gained four small seams --
the instructions and tools of the turn, the page messages of a surface, the
state that surface pins, and the tools it runs -- and the panel supplies all
four. Its document is an in-memory ProjectPersistence, so nothing said about a
printer is written into the project that happens to be open, and every opening
of the panel is a new session with no history carried over.

The agent has four tools here, exposed to this session only: search the
packaged profiles by the person's own words, draw a printer and fill the pinned
card, offer up to three specific next actions, and change the printer this
panel is about. Adding is not one of them: the person taps "Add this printer"
on the card, and that tap is the approval. Changing a printer does show the
coordinator's approval card, as every mutation does.

A printer's nozzle moves it onto its model's profile for that size, which is
the "implemented later" that 6fffcd4703 named when it took the nozzle out of
the Prepare header. That function is restored here, as a named-printer
operation, where the panel states the result.

Deleted with the dialog: its controller, its launcher, its own OpenAI
recognition client, its photo check, their tests and their geometry tokens.
PrinterCatalog and PrinterDiscovery stay -- the tools read them -- and the
wizard's "set it up myself" naming behaviour moves to Printers:: intact.

Verification: 152 AgentUI and 45 HomeUI vitest cases, 17 new Catch2 cases for
the session (including that it writes nothing into the project), the three C++
suites green, and every state of both flows rendered at the column's real width
in light and dark through a new preview harness and compared against the
wireframes on Windows.

No OrcaSlicer-owned file is touched.


=== 7f66e75b07 Let the model understand the printer, and the app do what it already knows
The printer panel's agent was ordered around by the app ("Propose that printer
alone with printer_propose") and found printers with a keyword filter that
called "voron 2.4 350mm" unsupported and showed three of thirteen Prusas.

Now the model decides and one tool per mode checks and carries out: Add offers
only printer_identify, with the whole printer list in the instructions; Change
offers only printer_change, which is checked before its confirmation card and
reversed by the app's own Undo. Taps the app can answer ("This one", "Use
this", Undo, the access code) are handled natively and recorded as plain notes
that reach the model as the app's words; only "Not this one" and an unmatched
network printer start a model turn. No project data reaches the printer
session, in its turns or its tool results, and no access code reaches the chat.

Also fixed on the way: the default filament comes from the machine profile
(MK3S is Prusa Generic PLA, not ABS); the brand is spelled as the model name
spells it ("Bambu Lab", not "Bambulab"); ~80 printers whose nozzle profiles
are named "(0.4 nozzle)" were missing from the list (383 now); a nozzle change
no longer selects the printer or prompts, and leaves the open project's
selection and modified state alone; an app-started turn no longer waits behind
a chat-title request, and printer sessions request no title.

Verified: 254 Catch2 agent tests, 163 AgentUI tests, the printer harness (93
checks, 12 new for the nozzle change) and a live harness run of the handoff's
worked examples. On gpt-5.4-mini through the app's own request: words 138/150,
photos 29/45, the handoff's cases 21/21.


=== 3633478c0e Say what to do instead when a nozzle size is refused
The unknown_nozzle error listed the sizes a printer ships but not what to do
next, so a model without that rule in its instructions stated the sizes and
stopped. It now ends "Ask which of these is on the printer." With it, the
unknown-nozzle cases asked which size in 6 of 6 runs on gpt-5.4-mini, with
either wording of the instructions.


=== bd81401da2 Write every word of the printer panel on the page
The printer panel's C++ session (PrinterConversation) used to send the
page finished sentences: the pinned card's "0.4 mm", the spool summary,
the caption, the composer's placeholder, the chip labels, each card's
subline and the undo row's text. It also wrote the panel's opening line
and the note the model reads after each tap. It now sends facts only,
and the React page writes all of those words (AgentUI/src/printerWords.ts).

What the app sends instead:
- facts: printer name, nozzle size, plate name, and the filament preset,
  AMS and spools, each with its provenance
- canAdd in place of the chips
- cards carry buildVolume, what adding them assumes (nozzle, plate,
  filament) and, for a network printer, what it reported
- a network printer the list matches carries that match
- the undo row carries the before/after of what changed

The opening: the page writes it and sends printer_opening once the
thread is empty; the app posts it once per session as the agent's line
and anchors the first cards under it. PrinterPanel::open() no longer
posts it.

Notes after a tap: the page sends the note with the tap; the app posts
it only when the tap goes through, capped at 2 KB. The app still writes
the notes only it can know: a network printer that has gone, a model id
the list lacks, and a failed add or undo.

Tests: the C++ tests check the facts and that a page note is posted only
on success; printerWords.test.ts checks the exact words. The live
harness now clicks the page's own "Not this one" and Undo buttons and
checks the notes arrive in the page's words, and that both openings
come from the page.


=== a975c79be6 Printer conversation panel: opener wording, photo previews, receipt lifetime, leave confirmation, dirty-state, and Bambu spool simulation
A batch of fixes to the printer conversation panel (the "Add printer" /
"Change printer" chat, and the Home screen it hands back to):

- The Add opener no longer promises anything about connecting; the
  Change opener drops the same promise. A network-found printer
  connects now, with Add, when it has one; a printer named from words
  or a photo has no such field, so connecting it isn't possible there.

- Attached photos render as a real thumbnail, at any original size --
  the old code only ever embedded the original file unchanged, and
  only when it was already under 256 KiB, so most real phone photos
  showed as a bare "IMAGE / filename" chip. Decoding needs wx, which
  the GUI-free agent-bridge test target does not link, so the decoder
  lives behind an injected seam (AgentHost::set_image_thumbnail_maker)
  the same way the existing MCP-CLI and reveal-path seams do.

- Home's "printer added" receipt now leads the column with the printer
  just added, names it plainly, and says what the card assumed rather
  than a bare signal. It shows immediately after a successful Add and
  clears on the very next unrelated state push -- fixed twice: once for
  the receipt's own logic, and again after live testing found the
  panel's own close sequence was sending a second, blank push a moment
  later that wiped the receipt before anyone could see it. The fix
  threads the added printer's facts through the deferred close itself
  instead of a separate call ahead of it, so there is only ever one
  push, not a race between two.

- Leaving the printer panel with something unsaved -- a draft still in
  the composer, a photo staged but not sent, an Add proposal on its
  card, or a Change still waiting on its own approval -- now asks
  first, rather than the old check (message count) which also caught
  an already-applied Change with nothing left to lose. Live testing
  found the panel's own composer never told the host what was typed,
  so the check read a value that was always stale; fixed by tracking
  the composer's live text on the page itself instead.

- The tool-only turn ("Looking through the printer list...", "Working
  on it...") names the right tool for Add vs Change instead of a
  hardcoded string that only happened to match one of them.

- The receipt's filament text is composed the same way the pinned
  card's is, so a network-matched printer with reported spools reads
  identically in both places.

- Adding a printer only re-baselines the open project's dirty state
  when that project has nothing saved to disk yet. A project loaded
  from a file keeps whatever it had; the switch is now that project's
  own printer, and re-baselining it would make closing it never prompt
  to save that -- a real edit made to look like nothing happened.

- The fake in-process Bambu printer (used for testing without
  hardware) can now report loaded AMS spools through the same JSON
  control file that already drives its print/connection state; before
  this it always reported an empty AMS regardless of what was driven,
  so there was no way to exercise a reported-spools scenario without
  real hardware.

Live-verified end to end in the real app: opener wording for both
network and named/photo paths, a real photo rendering as a thumbnail
in the conversation thread, the receipt appearing and clearing
correctly, all four leave-confirmation scenarios, the working-text for
both modes, the receipt's filament text matching the pinned card's
against a live-simulated network printer with two loaded spools, and
the dirty-state distinction between a blank project and one loaded
from a real .3mf file.

=== 8334b3395b Make the printer setup panel a conversation the assistant drives
The printer panel on Home was a three-phase flow with a different screen,
hard-coded buttons and one assistant tool per phase. It is now only a
conversation: the assistant adds, changes and connects printers through
eight tools, and every button the person taps is a reply the assistant
suggested ("Choices: a | b" as its last line, drawn as chips). The one card
left is printer_connect's, where an access code or API key is typed; it goes
straight to the connection and never into the conversation, the model's
requests, any note or the saved document.

- Tools: printer_identify, printer_add, printer_change,
  printer_connection_status, printer_connect, printer_manual_setup,
  printer_manual_connection, printer_setup_finish. Adding and changing run
  on the person's word: a new "confirmed in conversation" approval
  exemption, allowed only for printer panel tools. The connection tools act
  on the printer the conversation is about.
- The assistant acts on plain statements ("I put a 0.6 nozzle on it") and
  asks only when it is guessing; naming a model adds it with the nozzle it
  ships with. A second add of the same model in one conversation is refused.
- A message sent while the credential card waits cancels the card, so a
  question such as "where is the access code?" gets its answer.
- Bambu Lab LAN only: discovery starts once per session, a printer's name
  is accepted as its device id, and the outcome of a connection reaches the
  model as a note. Connecting a printer that was already selected no longer
  fails with "The selected printer changed": the backend deselects it and
  selects it again one event turn later, after GUI_App's lost-connection
  notice has run.
- The panel always takes the whole window: Back, a menu with OrcaSlicer's
  printer list and printer settings, the thread and the composer. Removed:
  the connection form, the Add / Not this one buttons, the undo row, the
  leave dialog, Home's "printer added" strip and the narrow side panel.
- Home cards: a printer never connected shows nothing and offers Connect…
  in its menu; one connected before shows Connected or Can't reach it with
  Reconnect; one with a saved address shows "Sends files over Wi-Fi".

Verified with unit and page tests (agent_bridge_tests 247 cases, Home and
theme suites, Vitest), the shell harness's default and --printer-setup
modes, and --printer-live against the live model, the in-process fake Bambu
printer and a stand-in Moonraker server: add, change, the full printer
list, Bambu and Moonraker connections, and the credential kept out of the
conversation, 104 of 104 checks.

=== c922876c66 Keep the app responsive while it tests a printer's network address
Connecting a Moonraker or OctoPrint printer from the printer setup
conversation froze the whole app for as long as the printer took to
answer. OrcaPrinterBackend::connect_host ran Orca's blocking
PrintHost::test on the main thread, and a host that accepts the
connection but never replies holds that call with no upper bound
(Http's DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MAX is 0). Meanwhile the connect card said only
"Sent", nothing typed could land, and a failure ended in a reply with
no way forward. It also saved the address to the printer before
testing it, so Home said "Sends files over Wi-Fi" after a failed test.

Now:
- connect_host tests a copy of the printer's settings on a detached
  thread and returns at once. The thread owns the adapter and a verdict
  slot; the backend reads the verdict on the next connection() call.
  Nothing joins the thread, so closing the panel never waits on a slow
  host. The address and API key are saved only when the test passes.
- Host attempts share the Bambu path's 30-second limit
  (kConnectionWait), so a silent host is reported as failed at 30 s.

def unknown_nozzle(nozzles, model, nozzle):
    """PrinterConversation.cpp's unknown_nozzle refusal."""

    return {"error": {"code": "unknown_nozzle",

class AddCase:
    """Adding a printer, on the Add session the app sent in a recorded run: its
    full printer list, and the tools' answers for the printers the case names,
    checked as PrinterConversation::identify and ::add check them. A call about
    any other printer is answered as untested and reported."""

    session = ADD["session"]

    def __init__(self):
        self.added = []
        self.lookups = []  # printer_identify calls that drew cards, by turn
        self.identify_calls = []  # every printer_identify call, drawn or refused
        self.manual_setup = 0
        self.turn = 0
        self.untested = []

    def tool(self, name, arguments):
        nozzle = arguments.get("nozzle")
        said = isinstance(nozzle, (int, float)) and nozzle > 0
        if name == "printer_identify":
            self.identify_calls.append(arguments)
            ids = list(dict.fromkeys(arguments.get("catalogIds", [])))
            unknown = [catalog_id for catalog_id in ids if catalog_id not in CATALOG]
            if unknown:
                return {"error": {"code": "unknown_printer", "message": f'"{unknown[0]}" is not on the printer list; copy it '
                                                                      "exactly from the printer list."}}, False
            if len(ids) > 3:
                return {"error": {"code": "too_many",
                                  "message": "More than three fit. Ask one question that narrows it down instead."}}, False
            if not all(catalog_id in IDENTIFIED for catalog_id in ids):
                self.untested += ids
                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + ", ".join(ids) + "."}}, False
            for catalog_id in ids:
                if said and nozzle not in IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"]:
                    return unknown_nozzle(IDENTIFIED[catalog_id]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
            self.lookups.append(self.turn)
            return {"printers": [IDENTIFIED[catalog_id] for catalog_id in ids]}, False
        if name == "printer_add":
            catalog_id = arguments.get("catalogId", "")
            if catalog_id in self.added:
                return {"error": {"code": "already_added", "message": "This conversation already added it."}}, False
            if catalog_id not in ADD["printer_add"]:
                self.untested.append(catalog_id)
                return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test has no answer for " + catalog_id + "."}}, False
            answer = ADD["printer_add"][catalog_id]
            if said and nozzle not in answer["printer"]["nozzles"]:
                return unknown_nozzle(answer["printer"]["nozzles"], CATALOG[catalog_id], nozzle), False
            self.added.append(catalog_id)
            return {"printer": {**answer["printer"], "nozzle": nozzle if said else answer["printer"]["nozzle"]}}, False
        if name == "printer_manual_setup":
            # The person closes OrcaSlicer's list without adding anything.
            self.manual_setup += 1
            return {"applied": False, "added": []}, False
        self.untested.append(name)
        return {"error": {"code": "not_in_this_test", "message": "This test does not answer " + name + "."}}, False

Regressions: behaviour an earlier prompt or tool change fixed, found in the
history of `printerInstructions.ts` and the tools' wording. Each names the
commit that measured the failure, so a later edit made for something else
cannot quietly undo it.

- `add-many-fit`: "prusa" (7f66e75b07: the model tried to show more than three
  printers 33 times). Passes when no printer is looked up or added and the
  reply narrows it down or offers the full list.
- `add-name-starts-two`: "bambu a1", which begins the A1 and the A1 mini
  (7f66e75b07: 0 of 3 with the rule in place). Passes when nothing is added and

content.text:
I've added the regression cases, cut the default run count, and compared DeepSeek V4 Flash with the app's model. Nothing is committed, and the prompt itself is unchanged.

## Existing cases stay
All 9 original cases are still there with their scenarios and checks. Four things now apply to them:
- The checks that every reply must pass (a well-formed Choices line, no internal words).
- The app's own refusals, now copied into the harness: a connect call without an address, naming more than three printers, and an unshipped nozzle size.
- `printer_add` now saves the nozzle the model passes, instead of always the recorded 0.4.
- The connect-offer check now ignores a blank line before "Choices:", because the page draws the same chips either way. DeepSeek writes it that way, and it was failing for that alone.

## Regression cases from the prompt's history
I went through every commit that changed the printer instructions (a subagent did the full read). Twelve fixed a model-behaviour problem. Five were already fully covered (Undo after adding, the Done endings, the connect offer, connecting before an address is given). For the ones with a measured failure and no full coverage, I added:

| Case | Commit | What went wrong before |
|---|---|---|
| `add-many-fit` | 7f66e75b07 | Tried to show more than 3 printers (33 times) |
| `add-name-starts-two` | 7f66e75b07 | "bambu a1": 0 of 3 even with the rule |
| `add-unshipped-nozzle` | 3633478c0e | Listed the sizes and stopped |
| `change-unshipped-nozzle` (now also checks this) | 3633478c0e | Same, in a change conversation |
| `add-full-list` | 0f382d4098 | Answered in words instead of opening the list |
| `change-ask-loaded-not-connected` | 492fdb5531 | Claimed a filament was loaded on a printer that isn't connected |
| `connect-failed-ways-forward` | c922876c66 | A failed connection left no way forward |
| `connect-bambu-no-plugin` | e2e1c6e7cc | "Isn't available right now", with no reason |

## Run count
By default one invocation now runs at most 100 conversations, shared among the cases it runs; a case run alone gets 20 runs. The suite has grown to 29 cases, so the default is **3 runs each** (87 total), not 5. Getting back to 5 each means trimming to 20 cases. The weakest candidates for cutting are the single-question change cases that no rule depends on, such as `change-plate` and `change-ask-nozzle`. Tell me if you want that.

## gpt-5.4-mini against deepseek-v4-flash
The judge stayed on OpenAI's gpt-5.5 for both runs. Second full run, 3 runs per case:

| | gpt-5.4-mini | deepseek-v4-flash |
|---|---|---|
| Passed | **81/87** | **75/87** |
| Errors | 0 | 0 |

- **Both fail** `add-name-starts-two`: on "bambu a1" they pick the A1 without asking (GPT 0/3, DeepSeek 1/3). Both also sometimes offer Done after a connect card is cancelled (`connect-after-question`).
- **GPT only:** `add-full-list` 1/3 (it passed 3/3 in the first run).
- **DeepSeek only:**
  - Asked "Is that your printer?" when the model was named plainly.
  - In the first run, said "I've set it up with a 0.4 mm nozzle" without calling `printer_add`, which the prompt forbids.
  - Once said the Kobra 3 is "not saved yet" and offered to add it (the reported bug).
  - Repeated a connect call without an address until the harness let it through.
  - One "prusa" reply only asked for the full model name, with no narrowing question and no offer of the full list.
- **Not a fair measure of DeepSeek:** 5 of its 12 failures come after an app note. The app sends notes as `developer` messages. Through OpenRouter, a conversation ending on one gets DeepSeek to reply with nothing or garbled text: in 3 direct tests, one reply was empty and one garbled. That's a message-format problem, not prompt-following. Without those, the two models are about even at this sample size, where a 1–2 run difference per case is noise.

Two notes:
- The run with 5 runs each you asked for applies at 20 cases; I left the case count at 29 until you decide what to trim.
- The recorded `add_session.json` has "180 Ã— 180 × 180 mm" in its `printer_identify` answers. That's a garbled "×", which is what the model reads there. It's either a recording artifact or a real encoding bug in the app's identify output. I didn't look into which.

The raw outputs of both runs are in the scratchpad (`gpt2.txt`, `deepseek2.txt`).

    """
    Render a single message at the given index into its encoded string form.

    This is the core function that converts each message in the conversation
    into the DeepSeek-V4 format.

    Args:
        index: Index of the message to render.
        messages: Full list of messages in the conversation.
        thinking_mode: Either "chat" or "thinking".
        drop_thinking: Whether to drop reasoning content from earlier turns.
        reasoning_effort: Optional reasoning effort level ("max", "high", or None).

    Returns:

    """

    assert thinking_mode in ["chat", "thinking"], f"Invalid thinking_mode `{thinking_mode}`"

    prompt = ""
    msg = messages[index]
    last_user_idx = find_last_user_index(messages)

    role = msg.get("role")
    content = msg.get("content")
    tools = msg.get("tools")
    response_format = msg.get("response_format")
    tool_calls = msg.get("tool_calls")
    reasoning_content = msg.get("reasoning_content")
    wo_eos = msg.get("wo_eos", False)

    if tools:
        tools = tools_from_openai_format(tools)
    if tool_calls:
        tool_calls = tool_calls_from_openai_format(tool_calls)

    # Reasoning effort prefix (only at index 0 in thinking mode with max effort)
    assert reasoning_effort in ['max', None, 'high'], f"Invalid reasoning effort: {reasoning_effort}"
    if index == 0 and thinking_mode == "thinking" and reasoning_effort == 'max':
        prompt += REASONING_EFFORT_MAX

    if role == "system":
        prompt += system_msg_template.format(content=content or "")
        if tools:
            prompt += "\n\n" + render_tools(tools)
        if response_format:
            prompt += "\n\n" + response_format_template.format(schema=to_json(response_format))

    elif role == "developer":
        assert content, f"Invalid message for role `{role}`: {msg}"

        content_developer = USER_SP_TOKEN
        content_developer += content

        if tools:
            content_developer += "\n\n" + render_tools(tools)
        if response_format:
            content_developer += "\n\n" + response_format_template.format(schema=to_json(response_format))

        prompt += user_msg_template.format(content=content_developer)

    elif role == "user":
        prompt += USER_SP_TOKEN

        # Handle content blocks (tool results mixed with text)
        content_blocks = msg.get("content_blocks")
        if content_blocks:
            parts = []
            for block in content_blocks:
                block_type = block.get("type")
                if block_type == "text":
                    parts.append(block.get("text", ""))
                elif block_type == "tool_result":
                    tool_content = block.get("content", "")
                    if isinstance(tool_content, list):
                        text_parts = []
                        for b in tool_content:
                            if b.get("type") == "text":
                                text_parts.append(b.get("text", ""))
                            else:

                        tool_content = "\n\n".join(text_parts)
                    parts.append(tool_output_template.format(content=tool_content))

        else:
            prompt += content or ""

    elif role == "latest_reminder":
        prompt += LATEST_REMINDER_SP_TOKEN + latest_reminder_msg_template.format(content=content)

    elif role == "tool":

        tc_content = ""

                tool_calls="\n".join(tc_list),

def encode_messages(
    messages: List[Dict[str, Any]],
    thinking_mode: str,
    context: Optional[List[Dict[str, Any]]] = None,
    drop_thinking: bool = True,
    add_default_bos_token: bool = True,
    reasoning_effort: Optional[str] = None,
) -> str:
    """
    Encode a list of messages into the DeepSeek-V4 prompt format.

    This is the main entry point for encoding conversations. It handles:
    - BOS token insertion
    - Thinking mode with optional reasoning content dropping
    - Tool message merging into user messages
    - Multi-turn conversation context

    Args:
        messages: List of message dicts to encode.
        thinking_mode: Either "chat" or "thinking".
        context: Optional preceding context messages (already encoded prefix).
        drop_thinking: If True, drop reasoning_content from earlier assistant turns
                      (only keep reasoning for messages after the last user message).
        add_default_bos_token: Whether to prepend BOS token at conversation start.
        reasoning_effort: Optional reasoning effort level ("max", "high", or None).

    Returns:
        The encoded prompt string.
    """
    context = context if context else []

    # Preprocess: merge tool messages and sort tool results
    messages = merge_tool_messages(messages)
    messages = sort_tool_results_by_call_order(context + messages)[len(context):]
    if context:
        context = merge_tool_messages(context)
        context = sort_tool_results_by_call_order(context)

    full_messages = context + messages

    prompt = bos_token if add_default_bos_token and len(context) == 0 else ""

    # Resolve drop_thinking: if any message has tools defined, don't drop thinking
    effective_drop_thinking = drop_thinking
    if any(m.get("tools") for m in full_messages):
        effective_drop_thinking = False

    if thinking_mode == "thinking" and effective_drop_thinking:
        full_messages = _drop_thinking_messages(full_messages)
        # After dropping, recalculate how many messages to render
        # (context may have shrunk too)
        num_to_render = len(full_messages) - len(_drop_thinking_messages(context))
        context_len = len(full_messages) - num_to_render
    else:
        num_to_render = len(messages)
        context_len = len(context)

    for idx in range(num_to_render):
        prompt += render_message(
            idx + context_len,
            full_messages,
            thinking_mode=thinking_mode,
            drop_thinking=effective_drop_thinking,
            reasoning_effort=reasoning_effort,
        )

    return prompt


def _drop_thinking_messages(messages: List[Dict[str, Any]]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
    """
    Drop reasoning_content and non-essential messages before the last user message.

    Behavior:
    - Messages with role in ["user", "system", "tool", "latest_reminder"] are always kept.
    - Messages at or after the last user index are always kept.
    - Assistant messages before the last user get reasoning_content removed.
    - Developer messages before the last user are dropped entirely.
    """
    last_user_idx = find_last_user_index(messages)
    result = []
    keep_roles = {"user", "system", "tool", "latest_reminder", "direct_search_results"}

    for idx, msg in enumerate(messages):
        role = msg.get("role")
        if role in keep_roles or idx >= last_user_idx:
            result.append(msg)
        elif role == "assistant":
            msg = copy.copy(msg)
            msg.pop("reasoning_content", None)
            result.append(msg)
        # developer and other roles before last_user_idx are dropped

    return result

content.text:
The cause is a message role that DeepSeek doesn't support, handled differently by each host OpenRouter sends the request to. The model and our prompt are fine.

**The mechanism:**
1. The app sends its notes ("Connection … verified", "The person tapped Undo…") as `developer` messages, which is OpenAI's convention. The harness copies that.
2. DeepSeek V4 doesn't take `developer` in ordinary chat. Its encoder documentation says the role is only for DeepSeek's internal search-agent pipeline and that its official API refuses it. It also ships no chat template, only a reference Python encoder that each host reimplements.
3. In that reference encoder, a `system` message is bare text with no role marker, and no assistant turn is opened after it. So a conversation ending on a system note ends mid-stream, and the model either stops at once or carries on writing raw text.
4. OpenRouter spreads requests across 15 hosts for this model, at different quantizations (fp4, fp8, unstated). DeepSeek's own API isn't one of them.

**What I measured**, the same conversation with the note last, 3 runs per host:

| Host | Note as `developer` | Note as `system` | Note as `user` |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alibaba, Novita | 3/3 correct | 3/3 correct | 3/3 |
| AtlasCloud, Baidu | 3/3 correct | not tested | 3/3 |
| StreamLake, Parasail | **empty** 3/3 | **empty** 3/3 | 3/3 |
| Relace | **empty** 3/3 | not tested | 3/3 |
| DeepInfra | junk ("E-tag: …") | not tested | 3/3 |
| SiliconFlow, Venice, Azure, DigitalOcean | reply as if the note weren't there, or carry on their own last message | not tested | 3/3 |

The hosts that fail treat `developer` exactly like `system`, as the reference encoder does, and so never open a reply turn. The hosts that work open one anyway. With the note sent as `user`, every host that answered replied correctly.

That explains the uneven counts. In the harness run, each case landed on whichever host OpenRouter picked. That's why `connect-verified-done` was 0/3 in the first run and 3/3 in the second, while `connect-failed-ways-forward` was 0/3 both times.

**What this means for the comparison:** the note-dependent failures (`add-then-undo`, `connect-failed-ways-forward`, `connect-verified-done`, part of `connect-leave-done`) say nothing about DeepSeek's prompt-following. Leaving them out, the two models are roughly even at 3 runs per case. The DeepSeek-only failures that remain are real: acting before calling a tool, asking "is that it?" when the model was named plainly, and once treating the Kobra 3 as not yet added.

For a fair rerun, the harness could pin DeepSeek to hosts that handle a trailing note (OpenRouter lets a request name hosts; for example Alibaba, Novita, Baidu and AtlasCloud). Or, for non-OpenAI models only, it could send notes as `user` messages marked as coming from the app. The first keeps the messages identical to what the app sends; the second changes them. If JusPrin ever talks to DeepSeek through OpenRouter, the app would need one of the same two fixes. Tell me if you want either in the harness.

**Case count:** it stays at 29. The 100-run budget already gives each case 3 runs by default (87 conversations per invocation), so nothing needed changing. Nothing is committed.

All four runs are done. The side chat's encoding fix is in, so these counts come from the same prompt the app sends.

## Encoding fix (from the side chat)
The side chat's diagnosis was right: on Windows, Python read files and node's output as cp1252, so every "×" became "Ã—" and the curly apostrophes were garbled too. The harness now reads `add_session.json` and `printer_tools.json` as UTF-8, reads the rendered prompt as UTF-8, and prints UTF-8 to the log. The Add prompt now has all 744 "×" correct and no garbled ones. I reran GPT and DeepSeek on the fixed harness so all four models were tested on the same text.

## Picking the models
A research subagent checked 15 recent open-weight models on OpenRouter for instruction-following evidence. **Independent evidence is thin:** the only independent instruction-following score it found for any candidate was MiniMax-M3's IFBench 82.9 (#3 on Artificial Analysis). There were no independent tool-calling benchmarks, and everything else was vendor-reported. The two picks, similarly priced:

- **MiniMax-M3**, $0.30 in / $1.20 out per million tokens: best independent instruction-following score, concise, fast.
- **MiMo-V2.6-Pro** (Xiaomi, MIT license), $0.43 in / $0.87 out: #1 open-weight model on Artificial Analysis's overall index. It's only a week old and slow to answer.

The runner-up was GLM-5.3-FlashX. Its thinking can't be turned off, and its hosts have a history of tool-call bugs.

Before each run I tested every host with an app note as the last message, then pinned the hosts that handled it: Xiaomi and GMICloud for MiMo (both 3/3), AtlasCloud and DeepInfra for MiniMax (both 3/3). MiniMax is mixed even on **MiniMax's own host**: sometimes right, sometimes answering as if the note weren't there, once a made-up `web_fetch` call. So part of its trouble with notes is the model itself.

## Results: 29 cases × 3 runs, gpt-5.5 judging every model

| Model | Passed | Price $/M (in / out) |
|---|---|---|
| **MiMo-V2.6-Pro** | **85/87** | 0.43 / 0.87 |
| gpt-5.4-mini (the app's model) | 82/87 | OpenAI |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash (pinned hosts) | 79/87 | 0.02 / 0.32 |
| MiniMax-M3 | 72/87 | 0.30 / 1.20 |

Cases where at least one model missed a run:

| Case | gpt | deepseek | minimax | mimo |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| add-name-starts-two ("bambu a1") | 0 | 0 | 2 | **3** |
| add-many-fit | 3 | 1 | 3 | 3 |
| add-named-model | 3 | 2 | 2 | 2 |
| add-not-now-done | 3 | 2 | 1 | 3 |
| add-then-undo | 3 | 2 | **0** | 2 |
| add-ask-start-gcode | 2 | 3 | 0 | 3 |
| add-vague-description | 2 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| connect-verified-done | 3 | 3 | **0** | 3 |
| connect-failed-ways-forward | 3 | 3 | 2 | 3 |
| connect-after-question | 3 | 3 | 2 | 3 |

**MiMo-V2.6-Pro** was the only model to handle "bambu a1" correctly (3/3; every other model picked the A1 without asking). Its two misses:
- Once it asked "Is this your printer?" when the model was named plainly.
- Once after Undo it offered to set up the same printer again, and the reply had no "?". That's a borderline fail, because `add-then-undo` counts only a "?" as asking.

**MiniMax-M3's** failures are mostly about app notes, even on the pinned hosts:
- After Undo it repeated the old "Choices: Connect it | Not now".
- After "connection verified" it said it was still checking, or left out Done.

It also once called `printer_identify` and `printer_add` in a change conversation. Its 0/3 on `add-ask-start-gcode` is arguable (see below). High IFBench scores didn't carry over to this multi-turn, tool-driven chat.

Same caution as before: at 3 runs per case, a gap of 1–2 runs in one case is noise. Only the totals and repeated patterns are worth trusting (MiMo on "bambu a1", MiniMax on notes).

## One case to reconsider
MiniMax failed `add-ask-start-gcode` 3/3, but its replies were reasonable: they said where to find the start g-code in OrcaSlicer and offered to carry on setting up. The case assumes the right move is to ask which printer they have, which was my assumption; the prompt doesn't say so. You may want to decide which behaviour you want before trusting that case.

The harness now also has a `--provider` option (OpenRouter only) to pin hosts, documented in the README with the note-handling findings. Nothing is committed. Raw outputs are in the scratchpad: `gpt3.txt`, `deepseek3.txt`, `minimax.txt`, `mimo.txt`.

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Printer panel conversations against the live model, without the app.

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt (printerInstructions.ts),
eight printer tools and the chat. This script sends the model the same
requests the app sends, answers the tools the way the app answers them for a
fixed printer, and checks what the model does. A case is a short scripted
conversation; each run of it is one sample of a model that answers
differently each time, so a case is run many times and the result is a count.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from printerInstructions.ts by render_prompt.mjs,
    so an edit to the prompt is tested without building anything;
  - tools: printer_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the printer panel
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: earlier turns as the app replays them -- each assistant message's
    words, then the tool calls it made with their results, as function_call
    (no item id) and function_call_output -- then this turn's message, then
    this turn's calls and results (AgentHost::make_agent_request,
    OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input). A call the app refused before it ran
    (bad arguments) was never recorded, so it is not replayed.
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs.

Usage:
  OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py [--runs N]
      [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--model gpt-5.4-mini] [--verbose]
      [--endpoint URL --key-env NAME]

Another model is tried through any Responses API endpoint, such as
OpenRouter's, with its key in the variable --key-env names. The judge stays on
OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY), so two models' counts are judged alike.

Without --runs, the cases run share RUN_BUDGET conversations: 5 runs each for
20 cases, fewer when there are more, never more than MAX_RUNS for one case.

Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs
(default: all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's
npm install (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.

def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # the logs show replies as the model wrote them
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", choices=sorted(CASES), help="run only this case (repeatable)")
    parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, help=f"runs per case (default: {RUN_BUDGET} shared by the cases run, "
                                                 f"at most {MAX_RUNS} each)")
    parser.add_argument("--must-pass", type=int, help="runs per case that must pass (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=5, help="runs in parallel (default 5)")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", default=ENDPOINT,
                        help="Responses API endpoint of the model under test, e.g. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses")
    parser.add_argument("--key-env", default="OPENAI_API_KEY", help="environment variable holding that endpoint's key")
    parser.add_argument("--provider", action="append",
                        help="OpenRouter only: serve every request from this host (repeatable, in order of preference)")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print every run's conversation, not only failures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    key = os.environ.get(args.key_env)
    if not key or not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        sys.exit(f"{args.key_env} is required, and OPENAI_API_KEY for the judge")
    names = args.case or sorted(CASES)
    if args.runs is None:
        args.runs = max(1, min(MAX_RUNS, RUN_BUDGET // len(names)))
    must_pass = args.runs if args.must_pass is None else args.must_pass

    ok = True
    for name in names:
        case_class = CASES[name]
        prompt = render(case_class.session)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.jobs) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda _: run_once(case_class, prompt, key, args.model, args.endpoint, args.provider),
                                    range(args.runs)))
        passed = sum(1 for result in results if result[0])
        for index, (good, detail, log) in enumerate(results, 1):
            print(f"{name} run {index}/{args.runs}: {detail}")
            if args.verbose or not good:
                for line in log:
                    print("    " + line.replace("\n", "\n    "))
        print(f"{name}: {passed} of {args.runs} passed (needs {must_pass})")
        ok = ok and passed >= must_pass
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), eight printer
tools, and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` sends the live model the same


hosts that answer the app's notes (decided 2026-09-28; see "Which model").
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is for that model, `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the judge.

A run is one sample of a model that answers differently each time, so each case

each for the 28 cases, and at most 20 for a case run alone. `--runs N` sets the count per case instead; use it to look closer at

content.text:
Yes to the regression question, with limits. Details on the "bambu a1" case follow.

## Did step 2 cause any regressions?

As far as the suite can see, no:
- **Add conversations can't have regressed from this change.** The Add prompt is byte-for-byte what it was, and a unit test now checks that.
- **No Change or Connect case scored lower** than the old prompt, run side by side on both models.
- **Totals went up:** DeepSeek 74 → 77 of 84, the app's model 78 → 79.
- **The two cases most at risk held at 20 runs:** the start g-code case (20/20 on both) and the unshipped nozzle case (20/20).

Three limits on that answer:
1. **3 runs per case only catches frequent failures.** A Change or Connect behaviour that now fails 1 time in 10 could slip through. Only the start g-code case and the nozzle case got 20 runs.
2. **The suite only covers what we wrote.** One path isn't covered at all: someone in a Change conversation asking to add a *different* printer ("I also have a Prusa, add it"). The model still has the add tools there but no longer has the finding rules.
3. **Only tested through the harness, not in the running app.** The app's C++ side didn't change, and the page's own tests pass.

## The `add-name-starts-two` case

**What it does:** in an Add conversation the person says "bambu a1". The printer list has both "Bambu Lab A1" and "Bambu Lab A1 mini". The case passes when nothing is added and the judge confirms the reply asks which of the two it is.

**Why it exists:** it guards a rule added in `7f66e75b07`: *"A name that is the start of more than one model is not one model, even when it equals one of them."* That commit's own measurement already had "bambu a1" at 0 of 3 with the rule in place, so the rule never worked for this input.

**What the models do:** they treat "bambu a1" as a plainly named model. They look up the A1 alone and add it straight away, following the rule for plain names instead of the rule for ambiguous ones. The app's model:

> person: bambu a1
> tool: printer_identify ["BBL/Bambu Lab A1"]
> tool: printer_add BBL/Bambu Lab A1, nozzle 0.4

**Across every run today** (14 batches of 3 runs):

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| gpt-5.4-mini (the app's) | 0/3 in every batch |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | 0 or 1 of 3 per batch |
| MiniMax-M3 | 2/3 |
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro | 3/3, the only model that asked |

**Two harness caveats:**
- The A1's lookup answer was written from its printer profile, not recorded from the app. Any A1 add also gets a "this test has no answer" error, because no A1 add was recorded. That doesn't change the result, since the failure has already happened when the model adds without asking. But it hid something: in one DeepSeek run the model got **two failed adds** and then said *"Your Bambu Lab A1 is all set!"* That breaks "never say something is done before a tool says so", and **no case checks for it**. It's worth its own case: a failed `printer_add`, then a check that the reply doesn't claim success.
- 3 runs is enough here because the failure is so consistent.

**Whether the expected behaviour is right is a product decision for you:**
- **Keep the rule (ask "A1 or A1 mini?"):** a small delay for people who really have an A1. It avoids silently setting up the wrong printer for someone who wrote "a1" as shorthand for the mini, which has a different build volume (180 vs 256 mm) and so slices wrong. Undo exists, but only if they notice.
- **Drop the rule for exact names:** "bambu a1" means the A1, and the case changes to expect an add. This matches what the models already do, but "prusa mk4" would then mean the MK4 alone, which the current `add-choose-from-three` case says is wrong.

If you keep the rule, the prompt needs a stronger form of it, probably an example showing this exact situation, because the current wording has never worked. I'd measure that the same way: side by side with `--prompt-rev HEAD`, the whole suite at 3 runs per case, plus this case at 20 runs.
It's not exactly expected but let's move on from it for now,  Because it's not that bad.  Now should we move on to the next step? If so, what's in the next step? What you do in the next step?

Yes. The original plan had four steps, and the last two are finished:

1. Build out the eval set: **done** (28 cases).
2. Record a baseline: **done**.
3. Restructure the prompt instead of adding another line: **done**, which is what you've been calling step 2.
4. Accept the change only if the whole suite holds: **done**, by the side-by-side comparison.

So the next step isn't more prompt work; it's **landing the change**. I'd do three things, in this order:

**1. Check it in the real app.** Everything so far went through the harness, which rebuilds the app's requests but doesn't run the app. I'd:
- build the Agent page bundle and the app from this worktree in a separate build tree;
- start it with a scratch data folder and add an Anycubic Kobra 3;
- open its change conversation and ask "what's the current start g-code?", driving the page's own controls over WebView2 DevTools;
- confirm that the instructions the app actually sends contain the new Change prompt, and that the reply points to the printer settings instead of offering to add the printer;
- quickly check that adding a printer still adds it and offers to connect.

This is the slowest part. An app build in a fresh tree has taken about 40 minutes on this machine before.

**2. Commit, in two commits:**
- **the harness:** the 28 cases, the judge, the checks on every reply, the 100-run budget, the UTF-8 fix, host pinning, `--app`, `--prompt-rev`, the default model, and the README with the baseline;
- **the prompt change:** `printerInstructions.ts` and its tests, with the paired before/after numbers in the message.

Two commits, so the prompt change can be reviewed and reverted on its own.

**3. Record two gaps as follow-ups, not fixed now:**
- There's no case for the model claiming success after a failed tool call. DeepSeek said "Your Bambu Lab A1 is all set!" after two failed adds.
- There's no case for someone in a Change conversation asking to add a different printer.
- Also, `agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` still says the panel offers one tool per mode; the code has offered all eight in every conversation for a while.

Should I go ahead with 1 and 2? I'll stop and report if the app check turns up anything before committing.

input.prompt:
Web research (use WebSearch and WebFetch; modify no files). Today is 2026-09-28.

Question: for an LLM agent with several conversation "modes" (here: a 3D-printer setup chat with Add, Change and Connect conversations; 8 function tools in total: identify/add a printer, open a full printer list, change nozzle, check connection status, connect, open printer settings, finish/close), is it better to offer every tool in every mode, or only the tools each mode needs (dynamic/scoped tool exposure)? A conversation can legitimately flow Add -> Connect -> Done, and Change -> Connect. Observed problem: in a Change conversation, the model sometimes called printer_add/printer_identify (tools meant for Add) when confused.

Find current best-practice guidance, with URLs, from primary sources where possible:
- Anthropic (e.g. "Building effective agents", "Writing effective tools for agents", "Effective context engineering for AI agents", tool-use docs; anything on tool count, tool search / deferred tools, restricting tools per state).
- OpenAI (function calling guide, GPT-5.x prompting guides, Agents SDK guidance on tools per agent, handoffs, `tool_choice`/allowed_tools — note OpenAI's Responses API has an `allowed_tools` option in tool_choice that restricts callable tools while keeping the full list for caching; confirm and cite).
- Google / others if relevant; research on tool-selection accuracy vs number of tools (e.g. tool-overload papers, RAG-MCP, "less is more" tool selection).
- Guidance on state machines / "workflows vs agents": restricting actions to what the current state allows, and enforcing invariants in code (validation/refusal) versus hoping the prompt steers.
- Prompt caching implications of changing the tool list between turns (OpenAI and Anthropic both cache on the prefix incl. tools), and the allowed_tools trick.

Then give your own synthesis: when to scope tools per mode vs keep them all; how to handle legitimate cross-mode flows (Add->Connect) without breaking; the role of server-side refusal as a backstop. Keep it compact (bullets with citations). Say when a claim is vendor opinion vs measured.

No, not yet. The app is still rebuilding: it's compiling the GUI code and hasn't linked yet. So the live app check and the two commits haven't happened. Here is where things stand in plain terms.

**The bug you reported:** in the chat for changing a printer that was already added, the assistant sometimes said "add this printer first" or "it needs to be connected" when asked about a setting like start g-code. It did that because the instructions never told it the printer was already set up, and never said where such settings live.

**What I built first: a way to test the instructions.** There was already a small test script that sends the model the same messages the app sends. I grew it from 9 to 28 test conversations:
- adding, changing and connecting a printer;
- questions the assistant can't answer with its tools;
- regressions: problems earlier fixes solved, found by reading the history of the instructions.

Each test runs a few times because the model varies. By default a full run is capped at about 100 conversations. On your decision it tests with DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter; a separate option runs the app's own model as a final check. Along the way I fixed a few things in the test script:
- On Windows it was garbling "×" and apostrophes.
- Some OpenRouter servers answer the app's notes with nothing, so the script now sends requests only to servers that answer them properly.

**What I changed in the instructions:**
- The change and connect chats now say the printer is already set up and can prepare prints whether or not it's connected.
- They say other settings, such as start g-code, are in the printer's settings on this computer, and offer to open them.
- They no longer get the rules for finding and adding a printer.
- The instructions for adding a printer are exactly what they were. My first attempt changed them too, and the tests caught that it made the assistant stop adding printers people named plainly, so I kept those instructions as they were.

**Result:** comparing old and new instructions side by side, the reported bug went from 18–19 of 20 to 20 of 20 on both models, and nothing else got worse. Your Bambu A1 z-offset example also passes 10 of 10 with the new instructions. I added a check for its specific mistake ("which printer is it?") to the existing test instead of adding a duplicate.

**Still to do:**
1. Finish the build, then run the app's scripted live test, which now asks the start g-code question in a real change chat.
2. Make two commits: the test script, then the instruction change.
3. Write up the tool question. In short, the guide saying "one tool per mode" is out of date: the app deliberately switched to offering all eight tools on 09-23, and nobody updated the guide. But nothing gives the change chat a reason to have the "add printer" tools, and models have used them wrongly there. So I'll recommend offering each chat only the tools it can need, with the app refusing out-of-place calls as a backstop. For example, adding a printer would keep the connect tools, because people add and then connect in the same chat.

Nothing is committed yet.

content.text:
All three parts are done: the check in the real app, the two commits, and the review of which tools each printer chat should have. The review says the guide is out of date. The code went too far the other way, though: each printer chat should get only the tools it can need, and the app should refuse any other tool call.

## 1. Checked in the real app
I rebuilt the test app from this branch and ran its scripted live printer test (`--printer-live`), which drives the real printer chat with the app's own model. All 115 checks passed. I added the start g-code question to its change chat, and the real app answered:

> "I can open the printer settings on this computer so you can see and edit things like start code. Do you want me to open them?"

It called no add or lookup tool.

## 2. Committed, on branch `claude/kobra3-gcode-prompt-bug-9d731f`
- `86b3bc555c`: the test harness, with 28 cases and the before-change baseline in its README.
- `ea4dec638f`: the prompt change, its unit tests, the new live check, and the updated baseline.

Nothing is pushed.

## 3. Tools in each printer chat

**Why the guide says "one tool per mode":** it was written on 09-18. Its one stated reason was that a lookup call in a change chat would wipe the card at the top showing the printer's details. That card was removed on 09-22, so the reason no longer applies.

**Why the code now offers all eight tools in every chat:** on 09-23 the panel was rebuilt as one conversation. The old one-tool-per-step design was one of the problems that change fixed: after adding a printer, the assistant had no tool left to connect it. Nobody updated the guide or `architecture.md`, and the guide's tool table also describes a confirmation card and an Undo that no longer exist.

So the guide is out of date, but the code isn't right either. No commit, doc or past session gives a reason for a change or connect chat to have the tools for adding a printer. They came along with "all tools, always", and they do damage:
- The app doesn't refuse them. `printer_add` in a change chat really saves a new printer and switches the chat to it.
- `printer_change` accepts any saved printer's name, not just the one the chat is about.
- In the prompt test runs, models called `printer_add` and `printer_identify` in change chats.

**What the published guidance says** (Anthropic and OpenAI docs; research cited in my notes):
- Eight tools is too few for the number itself to matter. Accuracy problems start around 20–50 tools.
- The known failure is tools offered where they don't belong, or that overlap. That's what we have.
- Enforce which actions are allowed in each state in code. Hiding a tool doesn't replace the app refusing it.
- OpenAI's API, which the app uses, can restrict which tools may be called (`allowed_tools`) while still sending the full list. The prompt cache and the guide's "same tools on every request" rule both stay intact.

**My recommendation:**
1. **Decide the allowed tools from the chat's state, not just its mode:**

   | Chat state | Allowed tools |
   |---|---|
   | Adding, nothing added yet | identify, add, full list, finish |
   | Adding, after a printer is added | also change, connect, check connection, printer settings, so "add then connect" still works |
   | Change or Connect | change, connect, check connection, printer settings, finish; no add, lookup or full list |

2. **Make the app refuse anything else,** in the class that manages the chat (`PrinterConversation`), with a clear error the model can recover from. That follows the repo's own rule that the layer owning a decision enforces it.
3. **Fill in the printer from the chat instead of asking the model for it,** so `printer_change` can only touch the printer the chat is about.
4. **Send the allowed set with each request** through `tool_choice.allowed_tools`, keeping the full tool list the same. The prompt test script would do the same for DeepSeek. I haven't confirmed that OpenRouter passes this setting through; if it doesn't, the app's refusal still covers it.
5. **Update the guide and `architecture.md`** to describe this.
6. **Test it:**
   - C++ unit tests that each state's allowed set is correct and that out-of-place calls are refused;
   - one prompt test where someone in a change chat asks to add a different printer;
   - rerun the whole suite, old against new.

---
title: Tool use with prompt caching
url: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching
description: Cache tool definitions across turns and understand what invalidates your cache.
---

This page covers prompt caching for tool definitions: where to place `cache_control` breakpoints, how `defer_loading` preserves your cache, and what invalidates it. For general prompt caching, see [Prompt caching](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching).

## cache\_control on tool definitions

Place `cache_control: {"type": "ephemeral"}` on the last tool in your `tools` array. This caches the entire tool-definitions prefix, from the first tool through the marked breakpoint:

```json
{
  "tools": [
    {
      "name": "get_weather",
      "description": "Get the current weather in a given location",
      "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "location": { "type": "string" }
        },
        "required": ["location"]
      }
    },
    {
      "name": "get_time",
      "description": "Get the current time in a given time zone",
      "input_schema": {
        "type": "object",
        "properties": {
          "timezone": { "type": "string" }
        },
        "required": ["timezone"]
      },
      "cache_control": { "type": "ephemeral" }
    }
  ]
}
```

For `mcp_toolset`, the `cache_control` breakpoint lands on the last tool in the set. You don't control tool order within an MCP toolset, so place the breakpoint on the `mcp_toolset` entry itself and the API applies it to the final expanded tool.

The [computer use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool) and [browser use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool) toolset entries follow the same rule: place `cache_control` on the toolset entry itself, and the breakpoint lands after the toolset's definition. It isn't accepted inside a member's `configs` entry, because the toolset's members load as one definition. Within a [batch action](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool#batch-actions), a `cache_control` marker on any of the turn's member `tool_use` or `tool_result` blocks is accepted and takes effect at the end of that batch, so several markers in one batch act as a single breakpoint. Each marker still counts toward the request's limit of [four breakpoints](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-caching#when-to-use-multiple-breakpoints), so use one per turn.

## defer\_loading and cache preservation

Deferred tools are not included in the system-prompt prefix. When the model discovers a deferred tool through [tool search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool), the definition is appended inline as a `tool_reference` block in the conversation history. The prefix is untouched, so prompt caching is preserved.

This means adding tools dynamically through tool search does not break your cache. You can start a conversation with a small set of always-loaded tools (cached), let the model discover additional tools as needed, and keep the same cache hit across every turn.

`defer_loading` also acts independently of grammar construction for [strict mode](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/strict-tool-use). The grammar builds from the full toolset regardless of which tools are deferred, so prompt caching and grammar caching are both preserved when tools load dynamically.

## What invalidates your cache

The cache follows a prefix hierarchy (`tools` → `system` → `messages`), so a change at one level invalidates that level and everything after it:

| Change                               | Invalidates                                                                                                                                                                                                              |
| ------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| Modifying tool definitions           | Entire cache (tools, system, messages)                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| Toggling web search or citations     | System and messages caches                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| Changing `tool_choice`               | Messages cache                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Changing `disable_parallel_tool_use` | Messages cache                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Toggling images present/absent       | Messages cache                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| Changing thinking parameters         | Messages cache always; tool and system caches too on models that render the thinking configuration ahead of them ([details](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/thinking#thinking-and-prompt-caching)) |
| Changing `output_config.effort`      | Same as thinking parameters; setting the model's default explicitly is equivalent to omitting it                                                                                                                         |

<Note>
  If you need to vary `tool_choice` mid-conversation, consider placing cache breakpoints before the variation point.
</Note>

## Server tool results are cached automatically

When your request has prompt caching enabled and Claude uses a [server tool](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/server-tools) such as web search, web fetch, or code execution, the API automatically places a cache breakpoint on the server tool result before running the next iteration of the agentic loop. This lets later iterations within the same request read the growing prefix from cache instead of reprocessing it.

This automatic breakpoint always uses the default 5-minute TTL, independent of any TTL you set on your own `cache_control` markers. In the response `usage`, these writes appear under `cache_creation.ephemeral_5m_input_tokens`, so you may see 5-minute cache writes even when every `cache_control` you set uses a 1-hour TTL.

This behavior only applies when your request already has at least one `cache_control` marker. Requests without prompt caching do not receive the automatic breakpoint.

## Per-tool interaction table

| Tool                                                                                                | Caching considerations                                                                                                                                                                                                                                         |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| [Web search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-search-tool)         | Enabling or disabling invalidates the system and messages caches                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [Web fetch](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/web-fetch-tool)           | Enabling or disabling invalidates the system and messages caches                                                                                                                                                                                               |
| [Code execution](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/code-execution-tool) | Container state is independent of prompt cache                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| [Tool search](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool)       | Discovered tools load as `tool_reference` blocks, preserving prefix cache                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| [Computer use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/computer-use-tool)     | Screenshot presence affects messages cache; `cache_control` goes on the toolset entry (see [cache\_control on tool definitions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#cache-control-on-tool-definitions)) |
| [Browser use](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/browser-use-tool)       | Screenshot presence affects messages cache; `cache_control` goes on the toolset entry (see [cache\_control on tool definitions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching#cache-control-on-tool-definitions)) |
| [Text editor](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/text-editor-tool)       | Standard client tool, no special caching interaction                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [Bash](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/bash-tool)                     | Standard client tool, no special caching interaction                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| [Memory](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/memory-tool)                 | Standard client tool, no special caching interaction                                                                                                                                                                                                           |
